review_author: Codex/GPT bounded local integrity and scope review; no Fable runtime approval

approval_need.standing_authority: Owner delegation: Primary releases reviewed jobs within my authorized scope and budgets; ADR 0012 delegates per-job release to primary without per-job owner interaction. Current R14 scope authorizes one fresh source-only provider call.
approval_need.interpretation: This manually reviewed replacement performs the still-unmade authorized first provider call. Scope retry:false / automatic_retry:false remains binding on provider attempts; this verdict does not permit replay of a dispatched or uncertain provider call or reset a consumed native identity.
approval_need.not_an_explicit_recovery_grant: No user-specific recovery approval is claimed; eligibility is the reviewer interpretation of existing standing release authority applied to independently verified pre-dispatch failure.
approval_need.boundary: Only this exact proposal, with absent shared adapter run folder, retained old claim, same frozen payload and at most one provider call. Any provider dispatch/uncertainty, adapter-run existence, changed payload/budget/provider, claim reset or automatic/repeated recovery requires a new review and applicable authority; no blanket retry authority granted.

reservation_accounting.reason: The initial native claim preceded the adapter and its request/ledger; there is no adapter attempt debit or provider dispatch to add to the prior. The same one-call reservation funds the unmade operation; retaining two native manifest identities does not itself accrue two provider reservations/charges. Original claim and manifest reserve metadata remain immutable.
reservation_accounting.uncertainty_boundary: If evidence of initial adapter/provider dispatch or incurred debit emerges, stop and reconcile conservative debit before release.

access_recovery: Primary retained identity/smoke success without credential/ACL/executor changes; this audit did not reproduce or diagnose access. Precise root cause remains unresolved.
risks: Recovery may fail again before dispatch and consume its new native claim; this review supplies no automatic subsequent retry.
A repeated adapter run remains blocked by the unchanged exclusive execution/run claim once created, regardless of native job ID.
Provider output fit, compatibility and semantic completeness remain unverified; Fable source-reference assessment is required after an eventual output.
